sections.h2: Which Scioto County offices deal with property tax?
sections.html:
Three county offices share the work, all at 602 7th Street in Portsmouth. The Scioto County Auditor (Room 103, 740.355.8264) sets values and takes appeals and homestead applications, with counter hours from 8:00 am to 4:30 pm. The Scioto County Treasurer (Room 102, phone (740) 355-8272) sends the bills and collects the money. The Scioto County Recorder (Room 110) files the deed after the auditor has processed the transfer.

The treasurer's office describes itself as part of the county's check and balance system with the auditor. In practice that means you ask the auditor why a value changed and ask the treasurer what you owe and when.

sections.h2: How much did the latest triennial update change Scioto County values?
sections.html:
In its latest triennial update, required every three years, the auditor reports an average countywide value increase of about 26.4 percent. The office says the state requires sales-based values to land between 90 and 110 percent of market value, measured on three years of sales, and that climbing prices pushed values up to reach that band.

The auditor adds that state reviewers rejected the first set of tentative values and required resubmission using values deemed sufficient for approval. Values come from sales data, market trends and statistical analysis, not from a physical inspection of every house. Averages hide big swings between parcels, so check your own record against nearby sales.

Farmland owners should know that current agricultural use value rates are reset in a triennial year by the state, not by the auditor.

sections.h2: What is the Inflation Cap Credit on a Scioto County tax bill?
sections.html:
The auditor explains that House Bill 186 introduced an "Inflation Cap Credit" for qualifying school district levies. It prints on the bill as a separate line, and parcel-specific inputs make the amount differ from one house to the next.

  • If you paid your second-half bill before the credit was applied, you need not do anything.
  • Any overpayment carries forward and is applied to the next first-half bill.
  • Homeowners who pay through an escrow account at a lender need no action, according to the treasurer, who said it was working directly with lenders.

The state's implementation work delayed the second-half bills that year. Second-half real estate and manufactured home taxes were due August 20, 2026 as a result, a date now past.

sections.h2: When are Scioto County property taxes due and what is the penalty?
sections.html:
R.C. 323.12 gives two routes: pay the whole year by December 31, or pay half by that date and the balance by June 20. A payment is timely when the treasurer has it by the last day, or when the envelope bears a U.S. Postal Service postmark dated that day or earlier. Postage-meter marks from a private machine are not accepted.

The county can move a date, as it did for the 2026 second half. Always read the due date printed on your bill instead of assuming the statutory one.

Late payment rules from R.C. 323.12 and 323.121, Ohio Revised Code
EventWhat the statute says
First half unpaid after its due dateTen percent added to what remains of that half
Second half unpaid after its due dateA like 10 percent penalty on the balance of unpaid current taxes
Delinquent taxesInterest at the rate set under R.C. 5703.47, charged on set dates
Valid delinquent tax contract in forceNo interest while the contract stays in effect, and no second-half penalty on the covered current taxes

If you cannot pay, call the treasurer early and ask about a delinquent tax contract before the penalties build.

sections.h2: How do I challenge my Scioto County property value?
sections.html:
The complaint goes to the auditor. R.C. 5715.19 sets the cutoff at the later of two dates: March 31 of the next year, or the end of first-half collection. The auditor hands each filing to the board of revision, and a mailed one is dated by its postmark.

The auditor also invites owners who believe the market value is wrong to file a complaint form with supporting evidence. Good evidence includes:

  • a recent appraisal or closing statement for your own home
  • sales of similar nearby houses
  • repair estimates that show a defect lowering value
  • photos or a report of damage from a casualty

A repeat filing has a limit. Once you have filed on a parcel, the statute bars another complaint during the same interim period unless something changed afterward: an arm's length sale, a casualty loss, a substantial improvement, or an occupancy swing of fifteen percent or more.

sections.h2: Who qualifies for the Scioto County homestead exemption?
sections.html:
The auditor's page describes a state-funded break for homeowners who reach 65 in the year they first apply, or who are permanently and totally disabled. Applicants must own the house and call it their main residence as of January 1, and stay inside the state's income limits. The page posts four forms: one each for owners 65 and over, disabled persons, veterans, and surviving spouses of public service officers killed on duty.

The applicant's name must be on the deed, and only one application is allowed per property. A reduction, if granted, shows on the bill received the following January. A surviving spouse can qualify between ages 59 and 65 under conditions the page lists. Call 355-8224 or stop in at Room 103 for forms.

sections.h2: How are Scioto County taxes handled when I sell the house?
sections.html:
Before accepting an offer, get a payoff from the Scioto County Treasurer for the parcel, delinquent balance included. The title company uses that figure to set aside tax money from your proceeds at closing. The deed then goes through the auditor, who endorses the conveyance, and on to the recorder.

A homestead reduction belongs to the qualifying owner. The auditor's page says changes in ownership must be reported, and the statement of value the buyer files under R.C. 319.202 asks the seller whether the property receives a tax reduction or an agricultural-use valuation. It also carries a notice to the buyer about eligibility for the reduction.

sections.h2: What does the Census Bureau show about the Scioto County housing market?
sections.html:
Residents here include 3,949 veterans, and 20.6 percent are 65 or older. Nearly nine in ten residents (89.8 percent) lived at the same address a year before. QuickFacts logs 10 building permits for 2025, a 27.9 minute average commute, 88.8 percent high school completion among adults 25 and over, and 18.2 percent with a bachelor's degree or higher.

About two in three homes (68.4 percent) are owner-occupied, with a median value of $137,900. A county with this many residents past 65 has a lot of potential homestead filers, so the program is worth checking before you list.

faqs.q: When are Scioto County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The statutory dates are December 31 and June 20. The county moved the second-half 2026 date to August 20, and that date has passed. Check the date printed on your own bill.

faqs.q: Who sends the property tax bill in Scioto County?
faqs.a: The treasurer, in Room 102 at 602 7th Street, Portsmouth, phone (740) 355-8272. The auditor sets values; the treasurer mails bills and takes payment.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to file a valuation complaint in Scioto County?
faqs.a: Whichever comes later: March 31 following the tax year, or the end of first-half collection. The paperwork goes to the auditor, and the board of revision decides it.

faqs.q: What penalty applies if I pay late?
faqs.a: R.C. 323.121 adds 10 percent to an unpaid first half, and another 10 percent to the unpaid current balance once the second-half date passes.

faqs.q: Does the homestead exemption move to the buyer of my house?
faqs.a: No. It stays with a qualifying owner who lives in the home, and the auditor wants ownership changes reported. A buyer must qualify and apply separately.
